 Search The Site Red Hot Chili Peppers, Dressed as Rick Rubin, Induct Rick Rubin Into the Hall of Fame Red Hot Chili Peppers, Dressed as Rick Rubin, Induct Rick Rubin Into the Hall of Fame
 Corey Irwin Corey Irwin Published: November 15, 2026 Kevin Kane/Getty Images for RRHOF SHARE 
 TWEET 
 Rick Rubin was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on Saturday night, with some of his previous collaborators taking part in the honors.
 Neil Young , whose 2022 album World Record was produced by Rubin, spoke about the producer's unique talents. Among Rubin's skills, Young explained, is his ability to keep outside drama away from the studio. “The music is all that’s allowed in," the singer remarked. "The people that make the music are cared for because they’re recognized.”
 Following Young's introduction, Rubin took the stage and delivered a short but triumphant message: "You can't kill rock and roll. Thank you."
 Five Rick Rubins Take the Stage
 After the real Rubin exited the stage, five fake Rick Rubins -- aka  Red Hot Chili Peppers  dressed in masks, beards and hair that looked identical to Rubin's trademark look -- came out. The group then proceeded to rock through and incendiary rendition of their 1991 hit "Give It Away."
 "We love you, Rick Rubin," frontman Anthony Kiedis proclaimed at the song's end, as the crowd in attendance, including Rubin, gave the band a standing ovation.
 Rick Rubin's Incredible Resume
 Rubin -- who's groundbreaking career has included work with Beastie Boys , Rage Against the Machine , Jay-Z, System of a Down, Tom Petty , Weezer and many more legendary acts -- was inducted into the Hall via the Musical Excellence Award. The honor was created to recognize "individuals who have dedicated their lives to crafting influential, important music infused with originality, achieving a level of timeless distinction."
 READ MORE: Top 25 Rock Producers 
 With over 100 albums under his belt, Rubin is one of the most prolific and celebrated producers in the history of popular music. He helped guide eight of Red Hot Chili Peppers' LPs, including Blood Sugar Sex Magik (1991), Californication (1999) and Stadium Arcadium (2006).
